concept: Hash-table lookup: average versus worst case

challenge.scenario: A table uses chaining. Its hash function sends all 1,000 student IDs to the same bucket. The table still has plenty of empty buckets.
challenge.question: Does looking up an ID still take constant time? Explain what the lookup has to do.

challenge_criteria: Lookup may scan a chain of n entries and is O(n) in the worst case. Empty other buckets do not help because the hash still sends every ID to one bucket.

recovery.scenario: The teacher doubles the table from 1,000 to 2,000 buckets, but the same faulty hash function still maps every student ID to bucket 7.
recovery.question: A teammate says doubling the table fixes slow lookup. Do you agree? Explain what would actually need to change.

recovery_criteria: No, the crowded chain remains and lookup can still scan n keys, O(n). Change the mapping to distribute keys, or use an appropriate alternative bucket structure. Resizing alone does not fix the specified faulty mapping.
